items.title: Natural Gas Cash Prices Pop as Exports Surge, Production Maintains Modest Pace
items.summary: Physical natural gas prices on Monday started the new week as they finished the last — climbing on strong LNG demand, light production and pockets of cold weather.

items.title: Record LNG Demand Emboldens Bulls, Sends Natural Gas Futures Rallying Above $3
items.summary: Natural gas futures made major headway on Monday as weather forecasts tilted cooler, LNG demand hovered in record territory and production slowly recovered from an autumn pullback.

items.title: Late Autumn Warmth Keeps NatGas Storage Builds Strong, Spot Prices Under Pressure
items.summary: NGI is projecting the next US Energy Information Administration (EIA) Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report through the week ended Nov. 6 to show a 67 Bcf injection, down 10 Bcf from the previous week.

items.title: European Chill Bolsters US LNG Outlook as Asian Demand Softens
items.summary: Colder weather is set to lift European heating demand and support US LNG purchases as the region heads into winter with a looming storage shortfall.

items.title: Global Gas Prices Shed Some Risk Premium as Geopolitical Tensions Ease
items.summary: Global natural gas prices continued to fall Monday as efforts to end the wars in Iran and Ukraine gained traction.

items.title: Soaring LNG, HDDs Trigger Natural Gas Rally
items.summary: Bullish two-week forecast trends and record LNG feedgas demand catapulted December natural gas futures comfortably above the psychological $3.00/MMBtu threshold on Monday.

items.title: TC Energy Greenlights 2.4 Bcf/d of US Midwest Natural Gas Expansions
items.summary: TC Energy has approved two natural gas pipeline expansion projects totaling 2.4 Bcf/d of incremental capacity to meet growing power generation demand, including from data centers, across the US Midwest.

items.title: US LNG Growth Outlook Puts European Supply Rules in Focus
items.summary: US LNG exporters are poised to widen their global lead as European policymakers back a change in methane requirements and American suppliers press for greater certainty to support long-term contracts.
